argument: Refuted: the kit tags do not yet produce coherent combat strategy, because the tag vocabulary has no satisfaction rule and the floor attack is tagged for one-handed weapons only. 09:169 calls the four Basic cards the attacks every character can make, with no Discipline required, and names them the floor; 09:174 then tags Basic Melee to weapon:one-hand, and the tag list at 15:25 never says what satisfies a tag. A hero who spends two of six kit points on a two-handed armament (15:40), as the Unbalanced's recommended kit does (15:151), therefore has no basic attack at all: the one-hand tag is unsatisfied, the ranged cards want a bow, and the unarmed card wants empty hands. The three cards that do accept a two-handed weapon each demand Disciplines first, so the hero is left with the gear and without an attack. Nothing states whether a Versatile weapon counts for a two-hand tag either, leaving a Longsword user's legality under the tags undecided (15:213, 15:219). Model A has none of these problems, since the floor cards carry no Discipline gate, which is to say the choice of model decides whether the game's fixed floor exists for a whole class of kits. Ruling on t-02: if the tags are to be the permission mechanism, the kit system needs a satisfaction rule per tag and either a two-handed basic attack or an explicit line saying a two-handed weapon satisfies Basic Melee. Smallest insertion: one sentence in the tag list at 15:25 defining what satisfies each tag, and one Basic attack card tagged weapon:two-hand.

evidence.claim: The four Basic cards are declared universal and Discipline-free, so they are the floor every kit must be able to reach.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: the attacks every character can make, no Discipline required. They are the floor

evidence.claim: Basic Melee is nonetheless tagged to a one-handed weapon, which a two-handed kit never satisfies.
The tag list names eight tags and defines no test for satisfying one; the same paragraph says a card with no tag requirement carries no Kit field.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: A card that requires none of them carries no Kit field at all

evidence.claim: Versatile may be used two-handed and Two-Handed must be, and neither property is tied to the tag vocabulary, so tag satisfaction is undecided even for a Longsword.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Versatile, can be wielded two-handed (Longsword only)

evidence.claim: The two-handed armament is a legal, recommended kit line, so the case is reachable at character creation rather than hypothetical.
The brief's Light citation resolves: two-weapon fighting requires the Light property on the off-hand weapon, and the worked example runs through Basic Melee.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: The off-hand weapon must have the *Light* property

evidence.claim: Instrumentation: the one-hand tag appears in three places only, none of which defines satisfaction, so the gap is real and not defined elsewhere.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: weapon:one-hand -> 09:174 (Basic Melee), 09:245 (Cleave), 15:25 (tag list), 3 hits; no satisfaction rule found
